requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`. I did not read the implementation. I judged only from the test and the requirement text.

- **First result carries `instructions`, even with empty `matches`.**
  - The first successful `search_text` for "absent" returns no matches. The test parses the result and requires `instructions` to be a string.
  - A separate session, `fresh`, gets its first result from `search_text` for "hit", which has matches. The test asserts `hits["instructions"] == instructions`. This shows the field appears per session and with non-empty matches.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** A separate session, `peer`, makes its first call with `search_structure` and a pattern that matches nothing. The test asserts that `matches` is `[]` and that `instructions` equals the text-search instructions.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.** The first call in `session` is `search_text` with the invalid pattern "(", and the test asserts it errors. The next search, "absent", still carries `instructions`. This covers a failed text search only. No failed structural search is tested. The requirement says the rule is shared, and I do not see a separate obligation for structural failures, so I do not count this as a gap.
- **Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.**
  - After `peer`'s first result, a later `search_text` has no `instructions`.
  - In `session`, a later "hit" search after the first delivery has no `instructions`.
  - The `get_next_page` result from `fresh` (`rest`) has no `instructions`. So does the page `second` from `session`.
- **Content of the instructions.** The test asserts that the instructions contain phrases about closing every delivered search page, `finish_search`, tags for excerpts relied on without a separate source read, `used:[]` for an empty result, and not reading more source. These match the `finish_search.mcp.description` text that the requirement cites. Its separate `instructions.content` requirement is a different subject.

Each obligation has an exercising scenario and an assertion on the outcome, so I found no adequacy gap.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
